MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, FEBRUARY 3, 2020

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274 by CHAIR ZIGRANG.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioner’s Present:  Schachter, Scott, Medawar, Zigrang, Carman, Yoo, Edler

  Commissioner’s Absent:  None

  Staff Member’s Present:  David Wahba, Community Development and Public Works Director
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  PLANNING COMMISSION REORGANIZATION

  Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba noted that upon City Council’s
  approval of the 2020 Assignment List at the January 14 City Council meeting, Bridget Carman
  was named as the new Commission Chair and Rick Edler as Vice Chair.

  Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba thanked CHAIR ZIGRANG and
  presented him with a plaque for his service as Planning Commission Chair from February 2019
  to February 2020.

  CHAIR CARMAN thanked COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG for his leadership this past year.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES, DECEMBER 2, 2019.

  VICE CHAIR EDLER, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion to,

  APPROVE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF DECEMBER 2, 2019 AS
  PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  7.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  Planning Commission will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read
  by title only.

  CHAIR CARMAN moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT to,

  APPROVE ITEM 5A

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so moved.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  1
MINUTES, FEBRUARY 3, 2020
   8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-19-19; APPLICANT: MR. JONATHAN PARK;
  LOCATION: 42 CLUB VIEW LANE; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination to construct one and two-story additions to a two-story residence and the
  partial conversion of the existing second floor for a new accessory dwelling unit (ADU). A
  Minor Deviation is required to decrease the front yard area by less than 10% and for the
  encroachment of the proposed addition into the required front yard which does not project
  closer to the property line than the forwardmost building line.

  Associate Planner Thom provided a PowerPoint presentation summarizing the staff report for PA-
  19-19. The current proposal is 4,335 sq. ft. not including the ADU; the proposed ADU is 748 sq.
  ft. and is exempt from the home size. The roof height has been brought down by a few inches
  and the lot coverage is still less than 30% maximum.

  Associate Planner stated that staff is not able to support the project and recommends that the
  Planning Commission: 1) Continue this application (PA-19-19) to a date uncertain to address the
  Commission’s neighborhood compatibility concerns, and direct the applicant and staff
  accordingly; or 2) Deny the project.

  Jonathan Park, Project Architect, provided new plans to the Planning Commission with further
  revisions from the plans which were not included in the staff report. The total deduction is 404 sq.
  ft. as well as a reduction in lot coverage. The total square footage has been reduced from 5,468
  sq. ft. to 5,064 sq. ft. The deduction has been from the living room and second floor south east
  corner. The extended covered patio has been reduced by 9 ft. in length. The roof has been
  changed to a gable roof to bring the home to the original chalet style. The reason for the covered
  patio is for privacy from the street. The staircase landing will be on the open deck area and not
  towards the street. Mr. Park further explained how the massing of the house has been reduced.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if staff has reviewed the drawings presented by Mr. Park.
  Associate Planner Thom stated that staff has not reviewed the plans presented tonight by Mr.
  Park.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Wahba stated that ADU’s
  can be attached.
  COMMISSIONER’S SCOTT, MEDAWAR, and ZIGRANG expressed their concern with the plans
  which were presented compared to those included in the agenda packet which have substantial
  differences.

  Creighton Marcott, Rolling Hills Country Club Estates Homeowners Association, stated that he
  has reviewed the design and seen the silhouette and stated that the HOA has concern with the
  mass of the improvements, including the covered patio. Being that ADU’s are allowed, there is no
  issue with the ADU. On review of the plans, they feel it is overdeveloped for their tract and it would
  be the third largest of 67 homes in the neighborhood. The largest home is across the street from
  him and is on a double lot. Mr. Marcott inquired about the elevation relative to the existing roof
  line.

  Mr. Park stated that it would be increased by 2 ft.

  In response to a question by CHAIR CARMAN, Mr. Marcott stated that in the past, the Planning
  Commission and/or staff has asked applicants wanting to do improvements/remodels for their
  opinion or thoughts and have asked that immediate neighbors be notified. This is something that
  he would like to continue in the future.

  CHAIR CARMAN stated that there are many HOA’s in the community and some are formal and
  some are not. However, the hope is that projects stay within the parameters of what is allowed
  in the city. There have been many new projects introduced with styles that may not have been
  approved in the past.

  Mr. Marcott stated that he would like the city to assist in being informed of new projects and also
  recognize that they must be proactive in responding to projects and meeting new owners coming
  into the community.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  2
MINUTES, FEBRUARY 3, 2020
   In response to a question by CHAIR CARMAN, Mr. Marcott stated that the HOA has issue with
  the width of the proposed project and stated that the home is at the end of a cul-de-sac and
  disagrees with the privacy issue.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if RHCCE is an active HOA and if there are enforceable CC&R’s.
  Mr. Marcott stated that their CC&R’s have expired.

  Chang Lee, 11 Club View Lane, speaking on behalf of fifteen neighbors (copy of petition provided
  to Planning Commission) in the neighborhood. Since finding out about the meeting, he and his
  neighbors began exchanging e-mails with their concerns about the project. Mr. Lee stated that he
  has been involved with the HOA with Mr. Marcott. He stated that, personally, he is not against
  adding square footage to homes. However, he shared his experience with his neighbor who built
  an open patio and later covered it making it livable space. He also expressed his concern with
  the home being built from fence to fence and concern about parking with the addition of the ADU.
  Mr. Lee requested more information for him and his neighbors on ADU’s.

  CHAIR CARMAN stated that there is a Community Roundup tomorrow February 4 at 6:30 p.m.,
  which includes a discussion on the New State Housing Legislation.

  Barbara Riker, 37 Club View Lane, stated that she has seen the silhouette and stated that the
  proposed home looks massive and does not think it is compatible with the neighborhood and also
  has concern with parking.

  Suzy Seamans, 1 Peacock Lane, asked for clarification on the applicant and the owner of the
  property. Director Wahba clarified that the applicant on a project can be the owner or architect.
  She stated that she always understood ADU’s to be a freestanding building. COMMISSIONER
  SCOTT stated that ADU’s are permitted to be attached.

  Director Wahba clarified that this project is a second story addition which includes an ADU and is
  being reviewed for Neighborhood Compatibility. Second story ADU additions will continue to come
  before the Planning Commission for Neighborhood Compatibility and setback requirements.
  There will be a Community Roundup tomorrow February 4 at 6:30 pm and a Joint City Council
  and Planning Commission meeting specifically on the ADU Ordinance on Tuesday, February 11
  at 5:30 pm.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he is not concerned with the ADU or that the ADU is on the
  second floor. The issue in this case is Neighborhood Compatibility and the location of the ADU is
  not relevant.

  Ms. Seamans stated that the city does not allow overnight parking. It should be emphasized that
  overnight street parking is not allowed.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if parking restrictions are removed if public transit is
  located within half a mile. Director Wahba stated that with the new legislation, the City may still
  require parking depending on the number of bedrooms in the unit. There is no parking required
  for Junior ADU’s.

  CHAIR CARMAN encouraged the audience to get involved in upcoming meetings.

  Mr. Park stated that this project did not start with an ADU in mind and stated that the house
  inclusive of the ADU is not the biggest house in the neighborhood. The ADU is completely within
  the home and it is unfair to judge the house and parking issues. The intention of the homeowners
  is to use the ADU, when they retire, to bring another family to live with them.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that the Planning Commission is not judging the ADU and does
  not affect anything that he has to say about this project. They are solely looking at this for
  Neighborhood Compatibility.

  Mr. Park stated that he can assure that the covered patio will not be used for living space in the
  future.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER expressed his concern with receiving new plans on the night of
  the meeting and staff has not had an opportunity to review them. He also stated that they rarely

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  3
MINUTES, FEBRUARY 3, 2020
   get substantial objections from this number of neighbors. Neighborhood Compatibility includes
  looking at among other things, style and scale.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that choices were made which impact Neighborhood
  Compatibility substantially. House has frontage of 40’ today and this plan has a perceived frontage
  of 85’. The second floor, the perceived frontage is approximately 35’ and with heavy rooflines is
  going to approximately 80’. Because of the odd shaped lot, the Minor Deviation benefited in a way
  that it should not. Square footage of the outdoor room should be counted as square footage of
  the house. Since the living room and the exterior covered patio projects towards the street it gives
  the home an appearance of looking 85’ wide that has a 40’ frontage. The square footage of the
  outdoor patio should be included in the square footage of the house since it is an integral part of
  the architecture.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT added that there is a violation of the setback line at the right side of
  the garage at the roof line where it is not below 45 degree angle. The Minor Deviation to expand
  the living room is not in accordance with the perception from the street. For those reasons, he
  cannot approve the project.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the job of the Planning Commission is not to write policy
  and the Planning Commission works with staff to make sure that you get a property that works
  within the city’s parameters. Being that the revised plans were received tonight and there has
  been no review by staff, he cannot comment on this project and his proposal is to continue this
  project to provide staff with sufficient time to review the new plans.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that this lot has a lot of space to do a lot of things and building
  the house towards the front is just massing and cannot support this project.

  COMMISSIONER YOO stated that considering the timing when the new plans were presented,
  staff should have an opportunity to review the plans. There is concern from the community and
  the Planning Commission; the covered patio, in particular, seems to have a huge impact from the
  street. He recommended working with their neighbors to come to a solution that would work for
  the owners and the neighborhood. The ADU is not an issue. The concern is massing.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he is in agreement with the Commissioners and does not
  like getting plans the day of the meeting. He encouraged the applicant/homeowner to meet with
  the HOA since they clearly have an interest in this project. He also encouraged the HOA to learn
  about ADU’s, which in this case, is not part of the equation. He cannot approve the project tonight.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION PA-19-19 TO A DATE UNCERTAIN IN
  ORDER TO GIVE STAFF SUFFICIENT TIME TO REVIEW THE NEW PLANS AND
  ADDRESS THE CONCERNS OF THE COMMISSION.

  Ayes: Schachter, Scott, Medawar, Carman, Zigrang, Yoo, Edler
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain:

  9.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-191209; APPLICANT: KEITH JOHNSON;
  ADDRESS: 2266 CARRIAGE DRIVE; Major interior remodel, in conjunction with a
  995 sq. ft. one story addition, and a new 312 sq. ft. covered patio. The project will
  require a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-190278); three Minor
  Deviations for reduction of the front yard area (MD-190280), additions in the front
  yard which do not project beyond the forwardmost building line (MD-190281), and
  a single story addition built along existing, nonconforming side yard setback
  building lines (MD-190-282); and a Variance for portions of the covered patio which
  would maintain less than the required rear yard setback (V-190279).

  CHAIR CARMAN recused herself due to her proximity to this property.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  4
MINUTES, FEBRUARY 3, 2020
   Planning Manager Naughton provided a presentation on Planning Application No. PA-191209
  summarizing the staff report.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, 1)
  Open the Public Hearing; 2) Take public testimony; 3) Discuss the issues; 4) Close the Public
  Hearing; and 5) Adopt Resolution No. PA-190291, approving the project.

  VICE CHAIR EDLER opened the public hearing.

  Keith Johnson, Architect, provided a brief overview on the Spanish Colonial Revival style of the
  proposed project.

  Steve Anderson, 2304 Carriage Drive, stated that he has known the homeowner for about 15 year
  and is happy about them beautifying their home and is in support of the project.

  Patrick Barley, 2275 Carriage Drive, stated that he is in support of the project and it will be great
  for the neighborhood.

  Ernest Magana, 2201 Carriage Drive, stated that he has known the homeowner for many years.
  He stated that he went online to review the staff report and plans and stated that it will be a great
  project that will be a benefit to the neighborhood. He also commended the architect on his design.
  He also added that he understands that there may be concerns from some neighbors, however,
  this is a unique situation since the houses on Carriage Drive are at varying elevations.

  Joe Salzetti, owner 2266 Carriage Drive, stated that he is aware that his neighbor is having an
  issue with not being able to see the trees above his house and stated that half the side of his
  house is at the same setback as the proposed project.

  Nadine Jett, 2267 Carriage Drive, stated that she lives directly across from this project. Due to
  the homes being on a hill and a slope, she expressed her concern with privacy issues. Ms. Jett
  expressed her concern with the high roof line blocking her view to trees and Neighborhood
  Compatibility, stating that Spanish Revival style is not compatible with the neighborhoods’ Ranch
  style homes.

  Damon Rubin, 2252 Carriage Drive, stated that his home is adjacent to the proposed project. His
  objection proposes to extend a nonconforming setback an additional 24’ and would raise 2 ½ ft.
  When viewed from his property, it blocks the trees and the property looms over his property, which
  already sits above his property. The project when completed will be 5’ from the property when
  measured from the end of the roof line (the eave).

  VICE CHAIR EDLER closed the public hearing.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about the 5’ setback. Planning Manager Naughton stated
  that there setback measurements are taken from the edge of the building façade and there are
  allowable encroachments, such as roof eaves.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked how tall the building could be if it was 10’ from the property
  line. Planning Manager Naughton stated that it could be upwards of 14’.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about the lights and cameras. Planning Manager
  Naughton stated that requirements can be made on exterior lighting. However, residents do install
  security cameras and there is question whether the city can put restrictions on these cameras.
  Director Wahba stated that security cameras cannot be regulated by the city and security lighting
  usually only come on when motion is detected.

  Mr. Salzetti stated that he had cameras in the easement and a neighbor called to have them
  removed. He stated that the cameras have caught various crimes and captured problematic
  neighbors.

  Mrs. Salzetti expressed her concern with a difficult neighbor.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT complimented the architect on his design and keeping with the
  community. He stated that the other option in order to gain square footage is to add a second
  story which would cause a greater impact on views and privacy.
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  5
MINUTES, FEBRUARY 3, 2020
   COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR suggested that the window that looks out the neighboring property
  be glazed.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG concurred and stated that the applicant has made the best use of
  his lot.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTER agreed that this is a minimal impact to neighboring properties.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER EDLER to,

  APPROVE ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. PA-190291.

  Ayes: Schachter, Scott, Medawar, Zigrang, Yoo, Edler
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain: Carman

  Director Wahba stated that PA-190291 has been approved and there is a 20 day appeal period
  for this project.

  B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-200013; APPLICANT: CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; An Ordinance of the City of Rolling Hills Estates,
  California, adding Section 17.30.080 to Chapter 17.30 to the Rolling Hills Estates
  Municipal Code establishing a security plan requirement for large commercial centers in
  the city’s commercial general district.

  Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba summarized the staff report. He
  added that he wanted to clarify some misinformation and stated that a security plan is not public
  information. In addition, the security plan would be and administrative process.

  A discussion ensued regarding the origin of this request.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that rather than imposing an ordinance, he suggested to go to
  each of the commercial centers and amend their CUP agreement.

  Director Wahba stated that the Planning Commission, 1) Open the Public Hearing; 2) Take Public
  Testimony; 3) Discuss the Issues; 4) Close the Public Hearing; and 5) Adopt Planning
  Commission Resolution No. PA-200013, recommending City Council adoption of an Ordinance,
  adding Section 17.30.080 to the RHEMC.

  CHAIR CARMAN opened the public hearing.

  Courtney Medak, Individual, stated that most of the problems at the Promenade are from the kids
  who are dropped off at the mall and not picked up until after 10:00 p.m. Most of the vehicle break-
  ins have occurred to Equinox members who leave purses or electronic devices visible in their
  cars.

  A discussion ensued about the need to require a security plan.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that when the mall began installing security cameras, the
  problem simply moved to another parking structure. He does not believe that this is the right
  approach.

  Ms. Medak stated that the problem is not limited to the Promenade.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR suggested that the city should have a round table discussion with
  business owners to come up with an ordinance.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER added that the whole business district should be involved.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT suggested the Commercial Improvement District or the Chamber of
  Commerce to fund patrol vehicles for the business district.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  6
MINUTES, FEBRUARY 3, 2020
   Ms. Medak stated that there has been progress in involving the school district and PTA parents.

  CHAIR CARMAN closed the public hearing.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  TABLE THIS ITEM AND RECOMMEND TO CITY COUNCIL THAT THERE BE AN
  ACTIVE EFFORT TO INVOLVE THE CHAMBER, BUSINESS COMMUNITY, THE
  SCHOOL DISTRICT AND LIBRARY, AND THE SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT TO
  DISCUSS A SOLUTION TO THE SECURITY ISSUES IN THE COMMERCIAL
  DISTRICT.

  Ayes: Schachter, Scott, Medawar, Carman, Zigrang, Yoo, Edler
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain:

  C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-200016; APPLICANT: CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; An Ordinance of the City of Rolling Hills Estates,
  California, eliminating Chapter 5.64, of the City of Rolling Hills Estates Municipal Code
  pertaining to Temporary Use Permits and adding a chapter establishing a formal
  permitting process for special events in the City.

  Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba summarized the staff report.

  Director Wahba stated that Staff recommends that the Planning Commission, 1) Open the Public
  Hearing; 2) Take Public Testimony; 3) Discuss the Issues; 4) Close the Public Hearing; and 5)
  Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. PA-200016, recommending City Council adoption of
  an Ordinance, adding Chapter 17.78 to the RHEMC.

  CHAIR CARMAN opened the public hearing.

  CHAIR CARMAN closed the public hearing.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked for the most significant difference from what exists today.
  Director Wahba stated that it is the fees for various type of events; rather than the one-size fee of
  $600.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by VICE CHAIR EDLER to,

  ADOPT PLANNING COMMISSION RESOLUTION NO. PA-200016, RECOMMENDING
  CITY COUNCIL ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE, ADDING CHAPTER 17.78 TO
  THE RHEMC.

  Ayes: Schachter, Scott, Medawar, Carman, Zigrang, Yoo, Edler
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain:

  10.  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  ROOF MATERIAL STANDARDS

  Planning Manager Naughton thanked the Planning Commission for their work with the past Roof

  The Planning Commission had no issue with the colors presented and agreed to allow staff to
  make the decision on color based on the design of the home.

  - Equestrian Committee (2019: Zigrang)
